ORDER REMANDING PROCEEDING TO SOAH

This Order addresses the joint application of Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC
(Oncor) and LCRA Transmission Services Corporation (LCRA) to amend their certificates of

convenience and necessity (CCNs) to construct, own, and operate a proposed Bell County East-

 PUC Docket No. 59182 Order Remanding Proceeding to SOAH Page 2 of 4
SOAH Docket No. 473-26-10397

PUC Docket No. 59475

SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349

to-Big Hill 765-kilovolt (kV) transmission line. A proposal for decision was filed on August 20,
20206, by the State Office of Administrative Hearings (SOAH) in this proceeding. The proposal for
decision also addressed a limited set of issues common to this proceeding and Docket No. 59182."
The two proceedings were consolidated at SOAH on May 8, 2026, to the extent necessary to

address these common issues.”

I. Discussion

When a proceeding is referred to SOAH, the Texas Government Code requires the
Commission to “provide to the administrative law judge a list of issues or areas that must be
addressed.”? The law also provides that “the commission may identify and provide to the
administrative law judge at any time additional issues or areas that must be addressed.”4 The
Commission referred this proceeding to SOAH on March 30, 2026. In the order of referral and
preliminary order, the Commission included 21 issues and subissues for the administrative law
judges (ALJs) to address.> However, the proposal for decision does not address all of the issues
identified in the March 30, 2026, preliminary order. Specifically, the proposal for decision does

not provide recommendations on preliminary order issue numbers 11 and 13, listed below.®

11. Are the proposed transmission facilities necessary to meet state or federal reliability

standards?

13. What is the estimated congestion cost savings for consumers that may result from the

proposed transmission facilities considering both current and future expected congestion
